items.caption: History/diagnostics tile for the heat pump (key-figure header + daily view), sibling module of NRGDashboardPVMonitor. Automatically finds all heat pump instances via the shared 'heatpump' contract (HeishaMon, WPHub) - no manual linking needed.
If a contract field is missing (e.g. COP or outdoor temperature with a plain WPHub installation), the tile simply hides the respective key figure/curve instead of showing a zero reading.

Key-figure header + daily/weekly/monthly/yearly/total/custom view, optionally drawn with ECharts or Highcharts (form “Appearance”) - same architecture as the PV monitoring tile. Detail switches (compressor frequency, flow rate, hot water temperature, operating mode color coding) follow as the next expansion step.

items.name: HookInfo
items.caption: IPSView/popup: the tile also runs as a standalone web page at http://<Symcon-IP>:3777%s (auto-refresh every 30 s). In IPSView, place a WebView element on a popup page and enter this URL. Note: WebHooks can be reached on the local network without logging in.

items.name: StandaloneEnabled
items.caption: Enable standalone web page for browser and IPSView

Only needed if the tile is to run as its own web page (browser, IPSView). If you only use the tile in the WebFront, you can switch this off: then no WebHook is registered and access from outside is removed. Switching it off removes the existing entry.
✨ Details: The tile starts directly with today’s daily view including the day before yesterday/yesterday/today quick select - no empty start state.

✨ Detail (weekly schedule, 18.10.2026): with HeishaMon 1.39.0 and later the “Schedule” tab appears - a graphical weekly editor (Mon–Sun × 24 hours, 15-minute grid) for ECO / Normal / Comfort of the heating curve (zone 1 and 2, heating and cooling) and quiet mode. You paint segments with your finger or the mouse, days can be copied, and each channel and the whole schedule can be switched on and off. The schedule runs in the HeishaMon module (the unit itself cannot hold a schedule): when switched on, the planned value is sent immediately; when switched off, the last value set stays in place. A manual change applies until the next switching time, rules on the board can override the shift (a note is shown). The unit does not acknowledge anything: the status of each channel shows whether the value was accepted.

✨ Detail (quick buttons, 18.10.2026): in the “Heating curves” tab, three buttons ECO / Normal / Comfort set the heating curve shift to -5 / 0 / +5 K with one click (only in the unit’s shift mode, not in direct mode); next to them a bar switches quiet mode to Off/1/2/3. The unit does not acknowledge anything: the tile reads the value back and only then reports “confirmed”. Rules on the board can override the shift, a note is shown.

✨ Detail (heating automation, 17.10.2026): with HeishaMon 1.35.0 and later the “Automation” tab appears - it shows state, reason, outdoor and room values as well as the last and next switch, and lets you set the on/off threshold, minimum room value, cooling and the automation switch. Limits and validation come from the module (errors appear at the affected field); switching on asks first, because the operating mode can change immediately. “Feature in this installation” (enabled in the HeishaMon form) and “Automation” (your switch) are two different things. The tab shows rooms and humidity together with their source (found automatically, own selection or none found); “Cooling” can only be set if a humidity source was found. The selection is maintained in the HeishaMon form.

✨ Detail (outlier protection, 01.09.2026): a single faulty archive value (e.g. a communication error at a partner module) is now discarded instead of distorting the daily view or the energy balance - a generic implausibility limit (1 MW), not an installation-specific value.

✨ Detail (start the tour yourself at any time, 01.09.2026): a clearly visible “?” button at the bottom left of the tile shows the introduction tour again at any time - regardless of the saved “already seen” status. Intended for shared instances (e.g. a demo/showcase instance with one shared login for all visitors).

✨ Detail (no current measurement, 13.09.2026): if the heat pump source reports the time of its last real measurement (e.g. WPHub from contract 1.13) and that is more than 15 minutes ago, a yellow note “No current measurement since …” appears above the key figures - instead of silently showing stale values as current.
